gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Notebookcheck measured 2 h 10 min of movie playback from the Aurzen ZIP Pro in Normal mode and a 57-inch picture from 1.59 m, or that Gizmodo got only 'just over an hour' in Eco mode from the original ZIP, whose rating is up to 1.5 h.
standout_why: I compared against: the Notateslaapp 16-inch article (2026-06-05), which covers only the front screen and says nothing about the rear one; the ManualsLib copy of the 2025+ Model Y manual, page 11, which lists the rear touchscreen's controls and has no measured figures; and ChatGPT's answer, which gives only Tesla's 8-inch size and feature list. tesla.com/modely, the Tesla manual Touchscreen page, tesla.com/learn/introducing-new-model-y and the Consumer Reports road test all returned 403, so I judged those from ChatGPT's summary. No rival page mentions projectors, a measured runtime, or any named measurement of a rear-seat screen.
decides: For owners who would use the projector route (AutoCinema screen plus a projector), the measured runtimes decide the pairing. On Notebookcheck's timing the ZIP Pro gets through a full movie on battery (2 h 10 min in Normal; Gizmochina got about 2.5 h in Eco and Normal). Gizmodo's original ZIP stopped after about 45 min in Turbo and just over an hour in Eco. So we recommend the ZIP Pro, or the ZIP only when it's plugged into car power. The measured throw distance also matters. Notebookcheck got 57" at 1.59 m and Gizmochina 60" at 1.7 m, which works out to about 1.4 m of throw to fill a roughly 50-inch panel. For the factory Tesla rear screen and the add-on console displays, I found no named measurement, so the screen pick still rests on fit by model year and price.
